Rain does not fall so much as arrive, like a guest who never learned to knock. It came that Thursday with a velvet insistence, filling the gutters, darkening the stone, turning the whole city into a watercolor of itself. He stood beneath the awning of a bookshop whose name he could not read... the letters had worn away decades ago, leaving only the ghost of commerce. Inside, a woman was shelving volumes with the reverence of someone handling relics. He watched her through the glass. She moved like a sentence with no period, continuous and unhurried, as if time were a suggestion she had politely declined. The rain thickened. Umbrellas blossomed on the sidewalk, black and red and one magnificent yellow. He did not have an umbrella. He did not want one. Some moments deserve to be felt completely, without the thin membrane of protection we stretch between ourselves and the world.
